claude.sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

links.outcome: DRP detection performance of RAG-LLM versus LLM alone
links.effect: RAG-LLM performed better than LLM alone; DRP detection accuracy improved in several categories but at the expense of lower precision.
links.quote: RAG-LLM performed better compared to LLM alone.

links.outcome: Medication error detection: LLM-CDSS alone versus junior pharmacist plus LLM-CDSS co-pilot
links.effect: In co-pilot mode, accuracy, recall, and F1 scores were optimized, with notable improvements in detecting severe DRPs.
links.quote: This study established that a RAG-LLM based CDSS significantly boosts the accuracy of medication error identification when used alongside junior pharmacists (co-pilot), with notable improvements in detecting severe DRPs.

screen.practice: retrieval augmented generation and human-in-the-loop co-pilot deployment
screen.reason: The study evaluates adding retrieval augmentation (RAG) to LLMs and compares fully autonomous deployment versus a human-in-the-loop co-pilot mode (junior pharmacist + LLM) for medication safety clinical decision support.
